authors: Aguirre Siliezar K, Patel S, Chande R, Joiner A, Hoover MC, Mathis MW, Hendrickson J, Siliezar J, Jankowski K
journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

mcqs.q: What was the primary reason most participants attended the two One Health Clinics?
mcqs.e: Most attendees came primarily for veterinary services (Clinic A 91%, Clinic B 75%).

mcqs.q: What did a majority of respondents report about their own health-seeking behavior?
o: They avoided care due to cost
They were more likely to seek their own healthcare when veterinary services were also offered
They trusted veterinarians less than physicians
mcqs.e: A majority at both sites said co-located veterinary services made them more likely to seek healthcare for themselves.

mcqs.q: The study concluded that co-located One Health Clinics can primarily serve as a tool to do what?
o: Enhance human healthcare access in underserved communities via veterinary engagement
mcqs.e: Authors concluded OHCs leverage the human-animal bond to boost human healthcare engagement in underserved communities.

authors: Orchard RJ, Scarbrough E, Crow A, Baldwin M, Moreau C

mcqs.q: In this veterinary-social service outreach model for unhoused people, the human-animal bond functioned mainly as what?
o: A catalyst for trust, engagement, and care continuity
mcqs.e: Thematic analysis framed the human-animal bond as a catalyst for trust, engagement, and care continuity.

mcqs.q: Beyond compassionate clinical care, what did the authors emphasize was needed for sustained success?
o: Trauma-informed delivery plus policy-level reform of structural barriers
mcqs.e: Findings stressed trauma-informed care and policy reform addressing structural barriers, not veterinary services alone.

authors: Schultz K, Alvarez E, Brooks J, Chun R

mcqs.q: What did the WisCARES needs assessment find low-income clients most frequently needed?
o: Pet food, supplies, dental/grooming items, and transportation
mcqs.e: Top reported needs were pet food, supplies, dental and grooming items, grooming access, transportation, and social-service navigation.

mcqs.q: What was the central conclusion about clients experiencing poverty?
o: They need more than basic veterinary care—wraparound support
mcqs.e: Authors concluded poverty-affected owners require wraparound support beyond clinical care, tailored to local needs.

mcqs.q: According to the paper, which structural changes limit veterinarians as One Health zoonoses communicators?
o: Companion-animal dominance, fee-for-service models, and corporate consolidation
mcqs.e: The author cites companion-animal practice dominance, fee-for-service, and corporate consolidation as constraints.

mcqs.q: How does the paper propose reconceptualizing the human-animal bond?
o: As a community-level resource akin to natural capital
mcqs.e: It argues the bond should be reframed as a community-level resource comparable to natural capital.

authors: Rejto N, Ramirez V, Fenelon HT, Xie M, Kuehl K, Terry A, Tin AH, Tabor E, Schneier K, Nee A, Richer A, Rabinowitz P, Meisner J
journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health

mcqs.q: What did over half of human clients at the Seattle One Health Clinic do?
o: Established healthcare for the first time in 2 years
mcqs.e: Over 50% established healthcare for the first time in 2 years.

mcqs.q: What proportion attended one or more non-emergency follow-up appointments within 2 years?
mcqs.e: 85% attended at least one follow-up within 2 years of their initial visit.

mcqs.q: The study concluded integrated human-animal care for homeless youth was what?
o: A feasible, acceptable model that promotes health-seeking
mcqs.e: Authors found the integrated model feasible and acceptable, promising for increasing health-seeking behaviors.

authors: Das M, Yustyniuk V, Perez AM, Perez Aguirreburualde MS

mcqs.q: Across the 70 included studies, dog rabies-vaccination uptake ranged how widely?
o: From less than 1% to over 90%, with none reaching full coverage
mcqs.e: Uptake ranged from <1% to >90% with no study reporting full coverage.

mcqs.q: Which factor showed a strong positive correlation with vaccination practice?
mcqs.e: Vaccination practice correlated strongly (r=0.69) with awareness of vaccine benefits.

mcqs.q: What were the common barriers to vaccination identified?
o: Lack of information, vaccine accessibility, and distance to clinics
mcqs.e: Barriers included lack of information, vaccine accessibility, distance to clinics, and personal constraints.

authors: Alvarez EE, Chun R, Brooks JW, Schultz K, Lygo-Baker S

mcqs.q: Beyond clinical skills, what did WisCARES students gain insight into?
o: Poverty, homelessness, and social determinants of health
mcqs.e: Students gained insight into poverty, homelessness, and social determinants influencing client decisions.

mcqs.q: Which interprofessional team members collaborated in this access-to-care clinic?
o: Veterinarians, veterinary nurses, and social workers
mcqs.e: The One Health team comprised veterinarians, veterinary nurses, and social workers.

authors: Monteiro HIG, Silva V, de Sousa T, Calouro R, Saraiva S, Igrejas G, Poeta P

mcqs.q: What role do companion animals play in antimicrobial resistance, per this review?
o: They are immune to resistant bacteria
They are reservoirs and vectors of multidrug-resistant bacteria that can spread to humans
mcqs.e: Pets act as under-recognized reservoirs and vectors of resistant pathogens shared with humans.

mcqs.q: What did the authors identify as a major obstacle to combating AMR in Europe?
o: Absence of a mandatory, uniform surveillance system
mcqs.e: The lack of mandatory, harmonized surveillance was cited as a key barrier to effective policymaking.

mcqs.q: Which overarching framework did the paper deem essential for AMR control?
mcqs.e: A One Health approach linking human, animal, and environmental health was deemed essential.

authors: Swedberg C, Siddiqi UR, Keshavamurthy R, Rana MS, Islam K, Kennedy E, Ross YB, Bonaparte S, Lohr F, Mursalin HS, Kamruzzaman M, Gamble L, Gibson AD, Blanton JD, Wallace RM

mcqs.q: What vaccination coverage threshold is needed for dog-mediated rabies herd immunity?
mcqs.e: Herd immunity for dog-mediated rabies requires ≥70% coverage.

mcqs.q: Which campaign strategy achieved the highest operational efficiency and coverage?
mcqs.e: eCVR led in efficiency (40.2 dogs/vaccinator/day) and average coverage (45%).

mcqs.q: What did post-vaccination surveys reveal about the dog population, limiting static-point methods?
mcqs.e: >93% of dogs were free-roaming and ~30% unowned, undercutting static-point strategies.

authors: Zhu T, Chang X, Wu X, Xia L, Zhu X, Zhu J, Li Z, Chen W, Fan Y, Tang Y, Liu J, Zhao H

mcqs.q: What persistent challenge did Shanghai's rabies program identify?
o: Low vaccination coverage among free-roaming animals
mcqs.e: The residual gap was low vaccination coverage in free-roaming/unowned animals.

mcqs.q: Which future tool did the program prioritize for free-roaming animals?
mcqs.e: Developing oral rabies vaccines was named a priority for free-roaming animals.

authors: Lider LA, Kiyan V, Seitkamzina DM, Ussenbayev A, Akmambaeva BE, Uakhit RS, Mannapova NE, Sytnik I, Bauer C

mcqs.q: What overall proportion of urban cats was infected with at least one GI parasite?
mcqs.e: 230/1,301 cats (17.7%) carried at least one intestinal parasite species.

mcqs.q: Which group had roughly double the odds of infection with several parasites?
mcqs.e: Kittens (<6 months) were ~twice as likely to test positive for T. cati, C. felis, and Giardia.

mcqs.q: Female cats had significantly higher odds (OR 1.8) of testing positive for which parasite?
mcqs.e: Female sex was associated with higher Giardia positivity (OR=1.8).

authors: Changalucha J, Anderson D, Yoder J, Stone B, Lugelo A, Kimera S, Lupindu A, Hampson K, Lankester F

mcqs.q: Why is mass dog vaccination considered more strategically valuable than human post-exposure prophylaxis?
o: It is always cheaper per person
It addresses the source of infection
mcqs.e: Unlike PEP, MDV targets the source of transmission, making it the most cost-effective control.

mcqs.q: Which delivery strategy was more efficient in rural settings?
mcqs.e: Community-led delivery vaccinated more dogs and was more efficient in rural areas.

mcqs.q: What was the authors' overall conclusion about the optimal delivery model?
mcqs.e: Both strategies are viable but optimal choice is context-specific (community-led rural, team-led urban).
